name: Promethium
nameMeaning: After Prometheus, who stole fire from the gods

zhRadical.note: The 钅(metal) radical — this element is a metal.

description: Promethium is the only lanthanide that is radioactive all the way through, and there is barely any of it on Earth — perhaps half a kilogram in the whole crust at any moment. It glows faintly in the dark and once powered luminous watch dials and tiny long-life batteries.
funFacts: There is thought to be less than a kilogram of natural promethium in the entire Earth's crust.
It is named after Prometheus, the Titan who stole fire for humankind.
Promethium glows with a pale blue-green light in the dark.
It was used in glow-in-the-dark watch dials before safer materials took over.
Tiny promethium batteries powered pacemakers and space instruments for years.

name: Samarium
nameMeaning: After the mineral samarskite, named for a Russian official

zhRadical.note: The 钅(metal) radical — this element is a metal.

description: Samarium makes magnets that keep working when things get very hot — up to 350 °C, far beyond what other magnets can handle. That is why they sit inside jet engines, electric guitar pickups and precision motors. Samarium was the first element named after a living person.
funFacts: Samarium-cobalt magnets keep their strength at temperatures that ruin other magnets.
It was the first element ever named after a person who was still alive.
Electric guitar pickups often use samarium magnets for a distinctive sound.
Samarium soaks up neutrons, so it helps control nuclear reactors.
Scientists use samarium-neodymium dating to measure the age of rocks and meteorites.

name: Europium
nameMeaning: After the continent of Europe

zhRadical.note: The 钅(metal) radical — this element is a metal.

description: Europium is the anti-forgery element. Euro banknotes contain europium compounds that glow red and blue under ultraviolet light, which is how cashiers spot fakes. Europium also made the red glow in old television screens and helps make white LED bulbs look warm.
funFacts: Shine UV light on a euro note and europium makes it glow — a hidden security check.
Europium gave old color TVs their bright red.
It is the most reactive of all the lanthanides, tarnishing quickly in air.
Europium is the softest rare earth — about as soft as lead.
Warm-white LED bulbs use europium phosphors to soften the harsh blue light.

name: Gadolinium
nameMeaning: After Johan Gadolin, a Finnish chemist

zhRadical.note: The 钅(metal) radical — this element is a metal.

description: Gadolinium is a superstar in hospitals: injected before an MRI scan, it makes blood vessels and tumours light up brightly so doctors can see them clearly. It is also the champion neutron absorber, and it has the strange ability to warm up when placed in a magnetic field.
funFacts: Gadolinium injections make MRI scans much easier for doctors to read.
It absorbs neutrons better than any other element, so it shields nuclear reactors.
Gadolinium is magnetic, but only when it is cooler than about 20 °C.
Placing gadolinium in a magnetic field makes it heat up — a possible future fridge technology.
It is named after Johan Gadolin, who started the whole rare-earth story.

compounds.about: Used in nuclear reactors and to make other compounds.

compounds.name: Gadolinium silicide germanide
compounds.about: Heats and cools in magnetic fields — magnetic refrigeration.

compounds.name: Gadolinium nitride
compounds.about: A magnetic semiconductor studied in research.

compounds.name: Gadolinium nitrate
compounds.about: Used to make phosphors and catalysts.

compounds.name: GdBCO
compounds.about: A high-temperature superconductor.

name: Terbium
nameMeaning: After Ytterby, the Swedish village

zhRadical.note: The 钅(metal) radical — this element is a metal.

description: Terbium glows a beautiful green, so it makes the green pixels in screens and the green in energy-saving light bulbs. It also does something remarkable: an alloy containing terbium changes shape in a magnetic field, which turns any flat surface into a loudspeaker.
funFacts: Terbium provides the green in fluorescent lamps and older TV screens.
Terfenol-D, a terbium alloy, stretches in a magnetic field and can turn a table into a speaker.
It is one of the four elements named after the tiny village of Ytterby.
Terbium is used in euro banknotes as another hidden anti-counterfeiting glow.
It is one of the most expensive rare earth metals.

compounds.name: Terbium aluminate
compounds.about: A crystal used to rotate laser light.

compounds.name: TGG

compounds.name: Terbium hexaboride

name: Dysprosium
nameMeaning: From Greek dysprositos, 'hard to get'

zhRadical.note: The 钅(metal) radical — this element is a metal.

description: Dysprosium was named 'hard to get' because it took its discoverer more than thirty attempts to separate it. Today it is genuinely hard to get for a different reason: electric cars and wind turbines need dysprosium to stop their magnets losing power when they heat up.
funFacts: Its name literally means 'hard to obtain' — it took over 30 tries to isolate.
Adding dysprosium keeps electric car magnets working when the motor gets hot.
It has one of the strongest magnetic pulls of any element at low temperatures.
Dysprosium is considered one of the most at-risk 'critical' elements for green technology.
It is used in the control rods that keep nuclear reactors steady.

compounds.name: Dysprosium oxide

compounds.name: Dysprosium nitride
compounds.about: A magnetic material studied for electronics.

name: Holmium
nameMeaning: From Holmia, Latin for Stockholm

zhRadical.note: The 钅(metal) radical — this element is a metal.

description: Holmium is the most magnetic element there is — it can be magnetized more strongly than iron. Because of that it sits inside the strongest laboratory magnets to concentrate their field. Holmium lasers are also used by surgeons to break up kidney stones without cutting.
funFacts: Holmium has the highest magnetic strength of any element.
Holmium lasers zap kidney stones into sand-sized pieces inside the body.
Its color changes depending on the light — yellow-orange in daylight, pink under fluorescent.
Scientists use holmium glass as a color standard to calibrate instruments.
It is named after Stockholm, the capital of Sweden.

name: Erbium
nameMeaning: After Ytterby, the Swedish village

zhRadical.note: The 钅(metal) radical — this element is a metal.

description: Erbium keeps the internet running. Every few dozen kilometers along the fiber-optic cables crossing the ocean floor sits a short length of erbium-doped glass that boosts the fading light signal back to full strength — without it, long-distance internet would not work.
funFacts: Erbium amplifiers keep internet signals strong across entire oceans.
Erbium turns glass and crystals a lovely pink color.
Erbium lasers are gentle on water-rich tissue, so dentists and skin doctors use them.
It is one of the four elements named after Ytterby in Sweden.
Erbium is added to sunglasses to give a pink tint.

name: Thulium
nameMeaning: From Thule, an ancient name for the far north

zhRadical.note: The 钅(metal) radical — this element is a metal.

description: Thulium is the rarest of the naturally occurring lanthanides, which makes it expensive. Its clever trick is being small: a pea-sized thulium X-ray source can go anywhere, letting doctors and engineers take X-rays in places a big machine could never reach.
funFacts: Thulium is the least abundant lanthanide found in nature.
Portable thulium X-ray units can be carried into the field.
It is named after Thule, the mysterious far-northern land of ancient legend.
Thulium lasers are used in surgery because they are absorbed strongly by water.
Euro banknotes glow blue under UV light partly thanks to thulium.

name: Ytterbium
nameMeaning: After Ytterby, the Swedish village

zhRadical.note: The 钅(metal) radical — this element is a metal.

description: Ytterbium has a party trick that engineers love: squeeze it and its electrical resistance shoots up. That makes it a perfect sensor for measuring the shock of earthquakes and explosions. Ytterbium atomic clocks are now even more accurate than cesium ones.
funFacts: Ytterbium clocks are so precise they would not lose a second in the age of the universe.
Squeeze ytterbium and it resists electricity more, making it a great pressure sensor.
It is another of the four elements named after Ytterby, Sweden.
Ytterbium fiber lasers cut through thick steel in factories.
It is one of the few lanthanides that is happy in a +2 charge as well as +3.

name: Lutetium

discovered.by: Georges Urbain and Carl Auer von Welsbach

nameMeaning: From Lutetia, the Roman name for Paris

zhRadical.note: The 钅(metal) radical — this element is a metal.

description: Lutetium is the last and the toughest of the lanthanides — the hardest and densest of the family. It was also the last of them to be discovered, after a bitter argument between chemists in three countries over who found it first and what to call it.
funFacts: Lutetium was the final lanthanide discovered, in 1907.
Three chemists claimed it at once, sparking a famous naming argument.
It is named after Lutetia, the Roman name for the city of Paris.
Lutetium crystals detect gamma rays in PET scanners that find cancer.
It is the hardest and heaviest of all the lanthanides.

zhRadical.note: The 钅(metal) radical — this element is a metal.

description: Hafnium is zirconium's near-identical twin — so alike that it took until 1923 to tell them apart. But in one way they are opposites: hafnium gobbles up neutrons while zirconium lets them pass, so submarines use hafnium control rods to switch reactors on and off.
funFacts: Hafnium and zirconium are so chemically similar they are extremely hard to separate.
Nuclear submarine reactors are controlled with hafnium rods.
Hafnium oxide made modern computer chips possible by replacing an older insulator.
Hafnium carbide has one of the highest melting points of any material, near 3,900 °C.
It is named after Copenhagen, where it was finally discovered.

name: Tantalum
nameMeaning: After Tantalus of Greek myth, who could never drink

zhRadical.note: The 钅(metal) radical — this element is a metal.

description: Tantalum is almost impossible to corrode — acids barely touch it — and it stores electricity brilliantly in tiny spaces. That is why a small tantalum capacitor sits in nearly every cell phone. It is also safe in the human body, so surgeons use it for plates and implants.
funFacts: Nearly every cell phone contains a tiny tantalum capacitor.
Named after Tantalus, who stood in water he could never drink — because tantalum refuses to absorb acid.
Tantalum does not react with body fluids, so it is used for skull plates.
Its ore, coltan, is mined in conflict zones, making sourcing an ethical issue.
Tantalum melts at 3,017 °C, one of the highest of all metals.

name: Tungsten

zhRadical.note: The 钅(metal) radical — this element is a metal.

description: Tungsten is the champion of heat: it melts at 3,422 °C, higher than any other metal on the table. That is why old light bulbs glowed with a thin tungsten wire. It is also incredibly dense — a tungsten cube feels shockingly heavy for its size, almost like gold.
funFacts: Tungsten has the highest melting point of any metal: 3,422 °C.
Old-fashioned light bulbs glowed because a tungsten filament got white hot.
Tungsten is nearly as dense as gold, so it makes fake gold bars and darts.
Tungsten carbide is so hard it is used to drill through rock and cut steel.
It is the only metal that some bacteria use in their enzymes.

description: Rhenium was the very last stable element to be discovered, in 1925 — every element found since then has been radioactive. It is one of the rarest things in the crust, and it has the second-highest melting point of all metals. Jet engine blades depend on it.
funFacts: Rhenium was the last stable element ever discovered on Earth.
The hottest parts of jet engine turbine blades contain rhenium.
It is one of the ten rarest elements in the Earth's crust.
Rhenium keeps its strength at temperatures that would melt most metals.
There is a volcano in Russia that puffs out pure rhenium sulfide.

name: Osmium
nameMeaning: From Greek osme, 'smell'

zhRadical.note: The 钅(metal) radical — this element is a metal.

description: Osmium is the densest element in the universe — a soccer-ball-sized lump would weigh as much as a small car. Its name means 'smell', because one of its compounds gives off a sharp, dangerous odor. Tiny osmium tips make fountain pen nibs and record player needles last for years.
funFacts: Osmium is the densest natural element; a cubic centimeter weighs 22.6 grams.
Its name means 'smell' because osmium tetroxide has a nasty sharp odor.
A blue-gray metal, it is one of the few that is not silver or gray-white.
Osmium tips on fountain pens and record needles resist wear for decades.
It is one of the rarest elements in the Earth's crust.

name: Iridium
nameMeaning: From Iris, the Greek goddess of the rainbow

zhRadical.note: The 钅(metal) radical — this element is a metal.

description: Iridium is the most corrosion-resistant metal known — nothing on Earth can rust it. It is also the clue that solved a 66-million-year-old mystery: a thin layer of iridium in rocks worldwide proved that a giant asteroid struck Earth and wiped out the dinosaurs.
funFacts: A worldwide layer of iridium in the rocks is the evidence for the dinosaur-killing asteroid.
Iridium is rare on Earth's surface but common in asteroids.
It is the most corrosion-resistant metal — even acid mixtures cannot touch it.
The official kilogram was once a platinum-iridium cylinder kept in Paris.
Iridium spark plugs last far longer than ordinary ones.

compounds.about: The starting point for most iridium chemistry.

compounds.name: Iridium dioxide
compounds.about: Used in electrodes that split water into hydrogen.

compounds.name: Iridium complex
compounds.about: Glows brightly; used in OLED phone and TV screens.

compounds.name: Iridium hexafluoride
compounds.about: A yellow, extremely reactive solid.

compounds.name: Chloroiridic acid
compounds.about: Used in plating and catalyst making.

compounds.name: Vaska's complex
compounds.about: A famous molecule that taught chemists how catalysts work.

compounds.name: Iridium sulfide
compounds.about: A rare mineral form of iridium.

compounds.name: Iridium carbonyl
compounds.about: A yellow cluster used in catalysis research.

compounds.name: Strontium iridate
compounds.about: Studied for unusual magnetic and electronic behavior.

compounds.name: Platinum-iridium
compounds.about: The alloy of the old standard kilogram and meter bars.

name: Platinum
nameMeaning: From Spanish platina, 'little silver'

zhRadical.note: The 钅(metal) radical — this element is a metal.

description: Platinum is rarer than gold and does not tarnish, which is why it is prized for jewelry. But its real superpower is chemistry: platinum speeds up reactions without being used up. It cleans car exhausts, helps make fertilizer, and a platinum drug fights cancer.
funFacts: All the platinum ever mined would fit in an average living room.
Spanish explorers threw platinum away, calling it annoying 'little silver'.
Platinum in car exhausts turns poisonous gases into harmless ones.
Cisplatin, a platinum medicine, cures most cases of testicular cancer.
A 'platinum record' award is more valuable than gold — just like the metal.

compounds.name: Cisplatin
compounds.about: One of the most successful cancer medicines ever made.

compounds.name: Chloroplatinic acid
compounds.about: Used to make catalysts and for plating.

compounds.name: Adams' catalyst
compounds.about: A brown powder chemists use to add hydrogen to molecules.

compounds.name: Platinum dichloride
compounds.about: Used to prepare other platinum compounds.

compounds.name: Cooperite
compounds.about: The main mineral platinum is mined from.

compounds.name: Platinum hexafluoride
compounds.about: So greedy for electrons it made the first noble gas compound.

compounds.name: Karstedt's catalyst
compounds.about: Used to cure silicone rubber for molds and seals.

compounds.name: Platinum on carbon
compounds.about: The catalyst inside hydrogen fuel cells.

compounds.name: Potassium tetrachloroplatinate
compounds.about: A red salt used to make cisplatin.

compounds.name: Sperrylite
compounds.about: A silvery mineral and important platinum ore.

name: Gold
nameMeaning: From Old English gold; symbol Au from Latin aurum

zhRadical.note: The 金 (gold/metal) radical — gold is the character all metal names are built from.

description: Gold never rusts, never tarnishes and never fades — a gold mask buried for 3,000 years comes out as bright as the day it was made. That permanence, plus its warm yellow shine, has made it precious in every culture on Earth. It is also astonishingly bendy.
funFacts: One gram of gold can be beaten into a sheet a whole square meter in size.
All the gold ever mined would form a cube only about 22 meters on each side.
Gold is made when neutron stars crash into each other in space.
Astronauts' visors have a whisper-thin gold layer to reflect harmful sunlight.
Gold is edible — gold leaf decorates fancy desserts and passes right through you.

compounds.name: Chloroauric acid
compounds.about: The dissolved form used for plating and making gold nanoparticles.

compounds.name: Gold(III) chloride
compounds.about: Red crystals used to make ruby-red stained glass.

compounds.name: Gold(III) oxide
compounds.about: The most stable oxide of gold, a brown solid.

compounds.name: Calaverite
compounds.about: One of the few minerals where gold is chemically combined.

compounds.name: Potassium dicyanoaurate
compounds.about: Used in gold electroplating baths.

compounds.name: Gold(I) chloride
compounds.about: A yellow solid used in chemistry research.

compounds.name: Gold sulfide
compounds.about: A rare compound studied by chemists.

compounds.name: Auranofin
compounds.about: A gold medicine used to treat arthritis.

compounds.name: Aurostibite
compounds.about: A rare gold-antimony mineral.

compounds.name: Purple of Cassius
compounds.about: Gold nanoparticles that turn glass a deep ruby red.

name: Mercury
nameMeaning: After the planet Mercury; symbol Hg from Greek hydrargyros, 'water silver'

zhRadical.note: The 水 (water) radical — mercury is a liquid.

description: Mercury is the only metal that is liquid at room temperature — a shimmering silver puddle that rolls into perfect beads. For centuries it filled thermometers and barometers, but mercury is a serious poison, so today it is being replaced almost everywhere.
funFacts: Mercury is the only metal that is liquid at ordinary room temperature.
It is so dense that an iron cannonball floats on it.
'Mad as a hatter' comes from hat makers who were poisoned by mercury fumes.
Mercury was once used in thermometers, but safer liquids have replaced it.
The planet, the metal and the Roman messenger god all share the same name.

compounds.name: Cinnabar
compounds.about: A brilliant red mineral, the main mercury ore and the pigment vermilion.

compounds.name: Mercury(II) chloride
compounds.about: Very poisonous; once used as a disinfectant.

compounds.name: Calomel
compounds.about: Used in old electrical reference cells and old medicines.

compounds.name: Mercury(II) oxide
compounds.about: Heating it releases oxygen — how oxygen was discovered.

compounds.name: Methylmercury
compounds.about: The dangerous form that builds up in fish.

compounds.name: Mercury fulminate
compounds.about: An explosive once used in the caps of bullets.

compounds.name: Mercury(II) iodide
compounds.about: Changes color from red to yellow when heated.

compounds.name: Dental amalgam
compounds.about: The old silver-colored tooth fillings.

compounds.name: Mercury selenide
compounds.about: Studied for infrared detectors.

compounds.name: Thiomersal
compounds.about: A mercury preservative once used in some vaccines.
